import pytest
from target import url_basename

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "url,expected",
    [
        # simple paths
        ("http://example.com/foo", "foo"),
        ("https://example.com/foo", "foo"),
        ("http://example.com/foo/", "foo"),
        ("http://example.com/foo/bar", "bar"),
        ("http://example.com/foo/bar/", "bar"),
        ("http://example.com/foo/bar?query=1", "bar"),
        ("http://example.com/foo/bar#section", "bar"),
        ("http://example.com/foo/bar/?query=1", "bar"),
        ("http://example.com/foo/bar/#section", "bar"),
        # multiple segments
        ("http://example.com/a/b/c/d", "d"),
        ("http://example.com/a/b/c/d/", "d"),
        ("http://example.com/a/b/c/d?x=1", "d"),
        ("http://example.com/a/b/c/d#frag", "d"),
        # path with dot‑segments
        ("http://example.com/../a", "a"),
        ("http://example.com/./a", "a"),
        # encoded characters (slash encoded as %2F should be treated as normal char)
        ("http://example.com/foo%2Fbar/baz", "baz"),
        # uppercase scheme
        ("HTTPS://EXAMPLE.COM/UPPER/CASE", "CASE"),
    ],
)
def test_url_basename_basic(url, expected):
    assert url_basename(url) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "url",
    [
        "",                     # empty string
        "http://",              # incomplete URL
        "example.com",          # missing scheme and slashes
        "http://example.com",   # no trailing slash after domain
        "http://example.com/",  # only domain with trailing slash
        "http://example.com?x=1",   # query without path
        "http://example.com#frag",  # fragment without path
        "http:///foo",          # malformed (missing host)
        "://example.com/foo",   # missing scheme
        "http://example.com//foo",  # double slash in path (no segment before)
    ],
)
def test_url_basename_no_match(url):
    # The function should return an empty Unicode string when the pattern does not match
    result = url_basename(url)
    assert isinstance(result, str)
    assert result == ""


def test_url_basename_type_and_unicode():
    # Ensure the return type is a Unicode string (str in Python 3) even for empty result
    assert isinstance(url_basename("http://example.com/foo"), str)
    assert isinstance(url_basename(""), str)
    assert url_basename("") == ""


def test_url_basename_invalid_input():
    # Passing a non‑string (e.g., None) should raise a TypeError from re.match
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        url_basename(None)


def test_url_basename_preserves_old_behavior_for_complex_paths():
    # URLs where the segment before the basename contains characters that could be a slash
    # (e.g., encoded slash). The old regex allowed any char except ? or #, the new one
    # disallows literal '/', but encoded '/' (%2F) is still allowed.
    url = "http://example.com/part%2Fwith%2Fslashes/last"
    assert url_basename(url) == "last"

    # Ensure that a literal slash inside the preceding segment (which is not a valid URL)
    # still results in no match, matching the old behaviour.
    url_invalid = "http://example.com/part/with/slash/last"
    # Both old and new regex should return empty because the pattern expects only one
    # optional segment before the captured basename.
    assert url_basename(url_invalid) == ""
